nodes.title: MODELS
widgets_values:
In my testing, WAN 2.2 TI2V 5B provides the best smoothing results at insane speeds. Sometimes it causes artifacts at the edge since it normally requires 704x1280 resolution and we are doing 720x1280, but I find the trade-off acceptable.

NOTE: You may replace this with WAN 2.2 T2V A14B-Low. It provides better results at significantly higher processing time. If you do this, you must also change the VAE to the WAN 2.1 VAE.

Do not use WAN 2.2 I2V A14B-Low, it actually performs WORSE than the T2V models in a V2V workflow.

nodes.title: IMPORTANT
widgets_values:
Your BLEND TARGET value MUST BE THE SAME as the number of overlapping frames from the VACE workflow. The default on both is 15 frames.

If you want to change the target fps to 30, you must change the frame multiplier to 2 for the same speed. If you keep the multiplier the same, you get smooth slow-motion.

nodes.title: INTERPOLATE
widgets_values: You may change the GIMM-VFI nodes with RIFE or FILM (or your preferred node). GIMM gives the best results for my use-case, but RIFE is much faster and pretty good quality.

nodes.title: START HERE
widgets_values:
1. Load your scene clip
2. Load your shift clip

This workflow will upscale both clips, smooth them with WAN 2.2 TI2V 5B, stitch them together, and interpolate to 60 fps.

nodes.title: SETTINGS
widgets_values:
Defaults:
- steps 8
- cfg 1.0
- sampler 'uni_pc'
- scheduler 'simple'
- denoise 0.1

nodes.title: REMOVE REDUNDANT FRAME
widgets_values: Since we added the first frame at the end, trim it here after interpolation

nodes.title: VERSION HISTORY
widgets_values:
v1.1
- correctly interpolates between the last and first frame
- swapped default GIMM VFI model from F to R (faster)
- attached GIMM VFI seed to workflow seed
- replaced "Load Video (Upload)" with "Load Video FFmpeg (Upload)"
- added image comparer for smoothing results (32nd frame)
- added ColorMatch after smoothing to correct shift due to VAE
- removed need to upload reference image for color matching
- replaced EasyColorCorrector with some manual nodes from LayerStyle

v1.0
- initial release

nodes.title: APPEND FIRST FRAME
widgets_values: We append the first frame to the end to ensure we generate interpolated frames between LAST FRAME -> FIRST FRAME transition (that is, when it loops)

nodes.title: COLOR CORRECTION
widgets_values:
Manual color correction. Stuff looks best when you (in my opinion) up contrast and saturation, lower brightness, and pull yellow bias out.

These take a while to run, but are more reliable than EasyColorCorrector. Upon investigation, that node didn't actually do very much (vibe coded nonsense).
